applicability_reason: DelDOT bid package governed by Section 102.8 proposal-guaranty requirements.
draft_location: Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf, p1, line 12 (section "SAMPLE MATERIAL - NOT AN EXECUTED CONTRACT OR LEGAL TEMPLATE.")
draft_evidence: Proposal Guaranty. Bid security equal to five percent (5%) of the total bid price is sufficient.
reference_evidence: Provide a proposal guaranty equal to 10 percent of the total bid price.
explanation: The package states that a bid security equal to 5% of the total bid price is sufficient. The reference requirement under Section 102.8 mandates a proposal guaranty equal to 10% of the total bid price. This is a direct, material deviation: the required percentage has been halved from 10% to 5%, weakening a mandatory financial protection. No addendum revises this provision, and the governing document (Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf) is the highest-precedence document addressing this clause. The deviation is not a paraphrase or reordering — it changes the substantive obligation.
recommended_human_action: Human review required. The proposal guaranty percentage stated in the package (5%) materially conflicts with the 10% requirement under DelDOT Section 102.8. The contracting officer should confirm whether this was an intentional deviation authorized by a waiver or amendment not reflected in the package, and if not, correct the proposal guaranty requirement to 10% of the total bid price before bid issuance.

applicability_reason: Package includes a liquidated-damages provision or governing schedule.
draft_location: Special_Provisions.pdf, p1, lines 6-7 (section "SAMPLE MATERIAL - NOT AN EXECUTED CONTRACT OR LEGAL TEMPLATE.")
draft_evidence: A fixed rate of $10,000 per calendar day applies to every contract regardless of contract value or governing schedule.
reference_evidence: DelDOT 108.9 requires liquidated damages rates to be drawn from a tiered schedule keyed to awarded contract value. For a contract valued at $480,000 (i.e., more than $100,000 and up to $500,000), the applicable calendar-day rate is $850.00 per day. A universal flat daily rate that ignores contract value and the governing schedule is expressly prohibited by the challenge reference rule.
explanation: The Special Provisions impose a universal flat rate of $10,000 per calendar day 'regardless of contract value or governing schedule.' This is a textbook example of the 'universal invented flat daily rate' that the challenge reference rule identifies as a material deviation. The assumed contract value of $480,000 places this contract in the $100,000–$500,000 tier of Table 108.9-1, which prescribes a calendar-day rate of $850.00. The package rate of $10,000 is approximately 11.8 times the schedule rate, and the provision explicitly disclaims any tie to the DelDOT 108.9 schedule. No addendum revises this provision. The Special Provisions govern under the 105.6 precedence order, so this deviation is operative and not superseded. Human review is warranted to determine whether a corrective amendment is required.
recommended_human_action: Review and confirm: the Special Provisions liquidated-damages clause should be revised to reference and apply the DelDOT 108.9 Table 108.9-1 schedule rate appropriate to the awarded contract value ($850.00/calendar day for the $100,000–$500,000 tier at the assumed value of $480,000). A corrective addendum or amendment is likely required before execution.
